definition: Archetypal analysis in statistics is an unsupervised learning method similar to cluster analysis and introduced by Adele Cutler and Leo Breiman in 1994.
details: Rather than "typical" observations (cluster centers), it seeks extremal points in the multidimensional data, the "archetypes". The archetypes are convex combinations of observations chosen so that observations can be approximated by convex combinations of the archetypes.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is Archetypal analysis — a small key that opens a big door.
